description: Design a 5-stage pipeline processor that implements a simple instruction set: ADD, SUB, AND, OR, and NOT. Each stage of the pipeline should consist of Instruction Fetch (IF), Instruction Decode (ID), Execute (EX), Memory Access (MEM), and Write Back (WB). The processor should support 2-input operations for ADD, SUB, AND, and OR, while NOT should work with a single input. The output of the processor should provide the result of the operation based on the inputs and the opcode of the instruction. The processor should handle hazards using a simple stalling mechanism.
code:
module pipeline_processor (
    input clk,
    input reset,
    input [3:0] opcode, // Opcode: 0000 - ADD, 0001 - SUB, 0010 - AND, 0011 - OR, 0100 - NOT
    input [4:0] src1, src2, // Source registers
    output reg [31:0] result, // Result output
    output reg valid // Output valid signal
);
    reg [31:0] reg_file [0:31]; // Register file
    reg [31:0] if_id_inst, id_ex_src1, id_ex_src2; // Pipeline registers

    // Stage 1: Instruction Fetch
    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            if_id_inst <= 0;
            valid <= 0;
        end else begin
            if_id_inst <= {opcode, src1, src2}; // Fetch instruction
            valid <= 1; // Set valid signal
        end
    end

    // Stage 2: Instruction Decode
    always @(posedge clk) begin
        id_ex_src1 <= reg_file[if_id_inst[9:5]]; // Decode src1
        id_ex_src2 <= (opcode[3:0] == 4'b0100) ? 0 : reg_file[if_id_inst[4:0]]; // Decode src2 (0 for NOT)
    end

    // Stage 3: Execute
    always @(posedge clk) begin
        case (if_id_inst[15:12]) // Instruction execution based on opcode
            4'b0000: result <= id_ex_src1 + id_ex_src2; // ADD
            4'b0001: result <= id_ex_src1 - id_ex_src2; // SUB
            4'b0010: result <= id_ex_src1 & id_ex_src2; // AND
            4'b0011: result <= id_ex_src1 | id_ex_src2; // OR
            4'b0100: result <= ~id_ex_src1; // NOT
            default: result <= 0;
        endcase
    end
endmodule

    input wire clk,
    input wire reset,
    output reg [1:0] state // 00: RED, 01: GREEN, 10: YELLOW
);

    parameter GREEN_DURATION = 2; // Duration for GREEN
    parameter YELLOW_DURATION = 1;// Duration for YELLOW

    reg [2:0] counter; // 3-bit counter
    reg [1:0] next_state;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            state <= 2'b00; // Start with RED

            2'b01: next_state = 2'b10; // GREEN to YELLOW
            2'b10: next_state = 2'b00; // YELLOW to RED
            default: next_state = 2'b00; // Fallback
        endcase
    end
endmodule

Each channel will have a request (REQ) and acknowledge (ACK) signal, and the DMA controller will grant access to one channel at a time based on a round-robin scheduling mechanism. module dma_controller (
    input clk,
    input rst,
    input req_ch1,
    input req_ch2,
    output reg ack_ch1,
    output reg ack_ch2,
    output reg status_ch1,
    output reg status_ch2
);

    reg [1:0] current_channel;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            ack_ch1 <= 0;
            ack_ch2 <= 0;
            status_ch1 <= 0;
            status_ch2 <= 0;
            current_channel <= 2'b00;
        end else begin
            case (current_channel)
                2'b00: begin
                    if (req_ch1) begin
                        ack_ch1 <= 1;
                        status_ch1 <= ~status_ch1; // Toggle status for channel 1
                        current_channel <= 2'b01; // Move to channel 2
                    end else if (req_ch2) begin
                        ack_ch2 <= 1;
                        status_ch2 <= ~status_ch2; // Toggle status for channel 2
                        current_channel <= 2'b10; // Move to channel 1
                    end

                2'b01: begin
                    ack_ch1 <= 0; // Clear ack for channel 1
                    if (req_ch2) begin
                        ack_ch2 <= 1;
                        status_ch2 <= ~status_ch2; // Toggle status for channel 2
                        current_channel <= 2'b10; // Move to channel 1
                    end

                2'b10: begin
                    ack_ch2 <= 0; // Clear ack for channel 2
                    if (req_ch1) begin
                        ack_ch1 <= 1;
                        status_ch1 <= ~status_ch1; // Toggle status for channel 1
                        current_channel <= 2'b01; // Move to channel 2
                    end
                end
            endcase
        end
    end

    input reset,
    input connect,

);

              CONNECTING = 2'b01,

            state <= IDLE; // reset to IDLE state

            case (state)

                    if (connect) state <= CONNECTING;

                CONNECTED: begin
                    if (disconnect) state <= DISCONNECTED; // Disconnected
                end
                DISCONNECTED: begin
                    state <= IDLE; // Reset to IDLE after disconnection

            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design a simple branch predictor using a 2-bit saturating counter. The predictor should take in the last branch outcome (taken or not taken) and update the counter state accordingly. The counter should have four states: Strongly Taken, Weakly Taken, Weakly Not Taken, and Strongly Not Taken. The branch predictor should output the prediction for the next branch instruction based on the current counter state.

module branch_predictor (
    input clk,
    input reset,
    input branch_outcome, // 1 for taken, 0 for not taken
    output reg prediction // 1 for taken, 0 for not taken
);

    reg [1:0] state; // 2-bit saturating counter

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            state <= 2'b10; // Start in Weakly Taken state
            prediction <= 1; // Initial prediction is taken
        end else begin
            case (state)
                2'b00: begin // Strongly Not Taken
                    prediction <= 0;
                    if (branch_outcome) state <= 2'b01; // Move to Weakly Not Taken
                end
                2'b01: begin // Weakly Not Taken
                    prediction <= 0;
                    if (branch_outcome) state <= 2'b10; // Move to Weakly Taken
                    else state <= 2'b00; // Stay Strongly Not Taken

                2'b10: begin // Weakly Taken
                    prediction <= 1;
                    if (branch_outcome) state <= 2'b11; // Move to Strongly Taken
                    else state <= 2'b01; // Move to Weakly Not Taken
                end
                2'b11: begin // Strongly Taken
                    prediction <= 1;
                    if (!branch_outcome) state <= 2'b10; // Move to Weakly Taken

            endcase
        end
    end

description:

00 - no shift,

10 - shift right, 
11 - rotate left.

code:

    input [7:0] data_in,
    input [1:0] control,
    output reg [7:0] data_out
);
    always @(*) begin
        case (control)
            2'b00: data_out = data_in; // No shift
            2'b01: data_out = data_in << 1; // Shift left

            2'b11: data_out = {data_in[6:0], data_in[7]}; // Rotate left
            default: data_out = 8'b00000000; // Default case
        endcase
    end
endmodule

module sample_rate_converter (
    input clk,
    input reset,
    input data_in,
    output reg data_out
);

reg [1:0] sample_count;

always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
    if (reset) begin
        sample_count <= 0;
        data_out <= 0;
    end else begin
        if (sample_count == 1) begin
            data_out <= data_in; // Output every second sample
            sample_count <= 0;    // Reset count
        end else begin
            data_out <= data_out; // Maintain previous output
            sample_count <= sample_count + 1; // Increment count
        end
    end
end

endmodule
